name: LtgSnapToMouseTab
src_typeComment: Snap To Mouse tab: with a GameObject selected, hover the Scene view and press a key — the selected object teleports to whatever real geometry the mouse currently points at. A one-shot action (not a held-key drag, not click-to-place) — press the key, the object jumps once, done.  3D-only, always raycasts real scene colliders — same reasoning as the Measuring Tape's 3D mode: a fixed-plane fallback would let the snap land somewhere with no real surface under it, defeating the point of a PLACEMENT tool (a measuring point can be abstract; a snapped-to prop shouldn't float).

src_members.name: TrySnapSelectedObjectToMouse
src_members.comment: Public so a self-test — or a hotkey/menu item bound differently later — can trigger a snap without a real Scene-view Event. Returns false (does nothing) if there's no selection or no collider under the given screen point, exactly like Measuring Tape's 3D mode rejects a miss rather than guessing.

src_members.sig: public static void SnapTransform(Transform target, Vector3 worldPoint, Vector3 surfaceNormal, bool alignRotation)
src_members.name: SnapTransform
src_members.comment: The actual transform math, pulled out as a static function so a self-test can drive it directly with synthetic points/normals — same reasoning as every other "extract the pure logic" split in this toolkit (LocomotionStateMachine.ClassifyState, DecalMeshBuilder.Build, ...): HandleUtility and a live Scene-view camera aren't available/meaningful in a headless batch-mode test.
